key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: The combined process offers a promising route to wear-resistant nickel-based protective coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel for mechanical and power engineering components.
method: Deposit NiCrFeBSiC coatings by detonation spraying, then laser remelt.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: Before/after testing showed porosity decreasing from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness increasing from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and specific wear rate decreasing from 2.864 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.447 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Laser remelting reduced coating thickness, and the approximately 3% decrease in corrosion current density indicates only modest corrosion improvement.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
